part: Mobile 390 — regulation detail (top bar, detail header, 2x2 action grid, vertical timeline, sticky section index, folded rail)
artboards: 03-regulation-detail (desktop); mobile-390 text spec (no 390 artboard PNG exists yet)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/DEVIATION-LOG.md 'MOBILE 390 SPEC' (Claude Design, delivered by the operator 2026-09-07), sections DETAIL HEADER / TIMELINE (vertical) / SECTION INDEX AND RAIL. No artboard PNG for 390 has reached the repo; the text spec is the binding source until one does, and when one arrives the image wins and the differences are logged.
notes: Same mount as compose-03-regulation-detail, at 390 instead of 1440 — the real AppShell frame wrapping RegulationDetailSurface, so the top bar and the detail surface are measured in one tree.

`compiledCss: true`, as on every mobile-* spec: the desktop/mobile switch in AppShell/Sidebar/TopBar is expressed as Tailwind utility classes. Opt-in per spec so the 1440 specs on this mount are not re-baselined.

The spec's 'Next obligation, N days' line: the build renders the desktop callout's own wording rather than inventing new copy, per the coordinator note carried in DetailShell.tsx's VerticalMilestoneStack header. Logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md.

The rail's prev/next links are not asserted: they render only when the URL carries list/pos/of and a neighbour slug, and this mount has no list position. The place-keeping card itself, which is what the spec requires to come FIRST in the folded rail, is asserted.

Logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md; the 390 artboard will state the date form the design intends.

children.note: UPDATED AT FOLD-61, because train 60's lane details60 changed what is correct here. mobile60 was cut from wave59, when the detail rail opened with the 'In this list' place-keeping card; details60 then fixed the rail order ONCE in DetailShell's slot contract so every detail surface opens with AT A GLANCE, which is what artboards 03/05/07/09 draw. The mobile 390 spec's own prose asks for the place-keeping card in the folded rail and it still renders, lower in the order; this row measures the FIRST card, so it follows the artboards rather than pinning the superseded order. Not a weakening: the same six properties are asserted, on the card that is now first.

forbid.name: no inline 'Ask about this' bar in the detail masthead
forbid.reason: Operator ruling P1 2.3: the scoped placeholder belongs in the masthead command bar, not a second bar; the action row follows the workspace tags row directly. At every width.

forbid.name: no floating Ask AI control
forbid.reason: Operator ruling P1 2.2: the masthead command bar is the ask; no floating control, at any width.

forbid.name: no band dropdown in the action row
forbid.reason: Operator ruling 3.1: the band is stated by the band pill in the header; changing it is not a reader action. Action row is exactly Export brief, Share, Watch, + Tag.

forbid.name: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
forbid.reason: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. Ruling 2.1 allows exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

boundsCheck.name: no top-bar cell overlaps a sibling or escapes the 56px bar at 390
boundsCheck.reason: Operator, 2026-09-07: 'your text is too right and it overlays different areas.'

boundsCheck.name: no action button overlaps another or escapes the 2x2 grid
boundsCheck.reason: Four 44px targets in a 2x2 grid at 390 is the tightest control cluster on the detail page.

boundsCheck.name: no timeline cell overlaps a sibling or escapes its row
boundsCheck.reason: The 62/14/1fr grid is the region the spec states most precisely; a label bleeding into the date gutter is exactly the collision class the operator's visual pass forbids. (:scope > span, so the dot's own nested marker is not compared against its parent cell.)
